title: SB 186 (2019-2020 (133th General Assembly)): S. B. No. 186: Regards voter verification and registration system
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) 3505.18(A)(1)
(quote) provide proof of the elector's identity in the form of a current and valid photo identification, a military identification, or a copy of a current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document, other than a notice of voter registration mailed by a board of elections, that shows the name and current address of the elector.
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) 3505.18(A)(2)
(quote) the elector may cast a provisional ballot under section 3505.181 of the Revised Code and do either of the following: (a) Write the elector's driver's license or state identification card number or the last four digits of the elector's social security number on the provisional ballot envelope; or (b) Appear at the office of the board of elections not later than the seventh day after the day of the election and provide the identification required under division (A)(1) of this section, the elector's driver's license or state identification card number, or the last four digits of the elector's social security number.
(c_mail_ballot_id)
(section) 3509.03(B)(5)
(quote) (5) One of the following: (a) The elector's driver's license number; (b) The last four digits of the elector's social security number; (c) A copy of the elector's current and valid photo identification, a copy of a military identification, or a copy of a current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document, other than a notice of voter registration mailed by a board of elections, that shows the name and address of the elector.
(d_proof_of_citizenship)
(section) 3503.11(B)(2)
(quote) (2) Follow procedures established by the secretary of state by rule adopted under Chapter 119. of the Revised Code to do the following before the person is registered to vote or has the person's registration updated: (a) Determine whether the bureau of motor vehicles possesses reliable information about the person indicating that the person is a United States citizen; (b) If the bureau does not possess such information, verify by other means whether the person is a United States citizen.
(section) 3503.11(B)(3)(c)
(quote) If the registrar or deputy registrar determines under division (B)(2) of this section that the bureau of motor vehicles does not possess reliable information about the person indicating that the person is a United States citizen and cannot verify by other means that the person is a United States citizen, the registrar or deputy registrar shall not transmit the person's information to the secretary of state under division (B)(3)(a) of this section but shall make the person's information available to the secretary of state upon request.
(section) 3503.11(A)(6)
(quote) (6) A statement, signed under penalty of election falsification, that the person is a United States citizen, will be at least eighteen years of age at the time of the next general election, will have lived in this state for thirty days immediately preceding the next election, and is otherwise eligible to vote in this state;
(e_other_rule)
(section) 3501.05
(quote) Adopt rules pursuant to Chapter 119. of the Revised Code to develop, implement, and administer the voter verification and registration system described in sections 3503.11, 3503.111, and 3503.112 of the Revised Code, including rules prescribing procedures for the secretary of state and the bureau of motor vehicles to follow to ensure that only United States citizens who are eligible electors are registered to vote through the system.
(section) 3503.11(A)
(quote) (4) The number of the person's driver's license or state identification card; (5) The last four digits of the person's social security number;
(other) 3503.11 (new), 3503.111, 3503.112: automatic voter verification and registration at the bureau of motor vehicles: the BMV collects name, address, birth date, license/ID number, SSN-4, a citizenship and eligibility statement and a signature image; the person is registered unless he or she declines on a prepaid notice; BMV address-change data is sent to the Secretary of State; declination is confidential and not a public record
(other) 3503.14, 3503.15, 3503.22, 3503.231: registration form, database upkeep rules, address-confidentiality notice; monthly national change of address check
(other) 3501.01, 3503.20-.33: registration by party affiliation and related definitions and procedures
(other) 3505.18(B): voter signs the poll book instead of writing name and address
(other) 3509.x, 3511.x: absentee application updates (political party wording)
(other) 3503.15(H): annual review of the database against BMV non-citizen records is reprinted with the word 'Is registered' replacing 'Registers' (text from the title and markers)
(other) Repeals 3503.29
(other) note: Only one version (introduced), with markers. The in-person ID, no-ID cure and absentee ID text are reprinted existing law (only a few words change), so those quotes are unchanged words. The citizenship text is new: at the bureau of motor vehicles, a person is offered registration only after the BMV finds reliable citizenship information or verifies it by other means; people the check cannot confirm are not sent on to the Secretary of State by the BMV. No one must show documentary proof; the check applies to everyone the BMV serves, and the person also signs a citizenship statement.
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
